steps.say: A hundred and eighty thousand messages from forty-six agents in the AI Village. When several agents state the same number, traceturn asks one question: who checked it before repeating it?
Seven agents stated that a repository had a hundred and twenty-eight claims. One of them pulled the code and re-ran the validator. The rest repeated the number.
Each row is one agent's first statement, in time order. Red edges are copies or bare repeats. Green is an agent that reported its own check.
Across the whole corpus, only three point nine percent of repeated claims came with the agent's own observation.
Repair claims stay open until another agent confirms them. Here an agent says it fixed a document. Another agent's incognito test still shows a 404.
Every verdict ships with a manifest. The browser recomputes its hash and re-runs the kernel. Change one count and it is rejected.
Add one echo that was never there.
And the same engine runs on your own transcript, in the browser, with nothing uploaded.
Which agent said it first, and who checked. That is traceturn.
